children: Egypt's annual headline inflation rate is expected to decline to 13.9% in September from 14.5% in August, with analysts citing favourable housing base effects that could offset pressure from food and utility costs, a Reuters poll ahead of data due on Saturday showed.
The median forecast of 16 analysts polled by Reuters between September 30 and October 7 was for annual urban consumer inflation to slip to 13.9%, with estimates ranging from 13.2% to 15.0%.

"We expect Egypt's headline inflation rate to fall from 14.5% year-on-year to 13.4% yoy in September," MENA economist Farouk Soussa at Goldman Sachs said in a note, adding that last year’s rise in imputed rents will fall out of the annual comparison.
Soussa said disinflation should accelerate in early 2027 if the Egyptian pound remains stable and energy prices ease.

While the average forecast was for lower inflation, Barclays' James Swanston expected inflation to increase to 15.0%, citing stronger food inflation and the continued pass-through from July electricity tariff increases.

Esraa Ahmed of digital investment platform Thndr said: “We expect some upward pressure from food prices, as well as from housing items, particularly rents. However, both have relatively favourable base effects – especially rents – which should partly offset their impact on the headline annual inflation rate."
Six analysts also provided forecasts for core inflation. The median estimate was 14.4% in a range of 13.9% to 15.2%.
Analysts say consumer prices remain vulnerable to further increases in fuel and electricity prices as Egypt continues subsidy reforms under its $8 billion IMF support package.
